youtube.title: RICHARD BARGE
youtube.summary: Rodney speaks with Richard Barge, Chair of the New Zealand Hemp Industry Association, about the potential of industrial hemp beyond its drug stigma and the regulatory barriers limiting its growth. They discuss current cultivation, processing challenges, and its wide applications in food, fibre, and health products. Richard highlights the need for investment, improved infrastructure, and regulatory reform to unlock hemp’s future in New Zealand. For further information: Visit the NZ Hemp Industries Association website Read the announcement on 11 December 2025 Check out the Ministry of Health Guidance The iHemp Catalogue and iHemp Bag campaign The Australian Industrial Hemp conference 2026

youtube.title: THE WILMS REPORT
youtube.summary: WARNING: This episode contains references to child rape, discretion advised Tim Wilms joins Paul to discuss major political and governance developments in Australia, including Angus Taylor assuming the Liberal leadership, Sussan Ley’s resignation and the resulting by-election. It also covers serious issues emerging in Victoria – allegations of corruption linked to the Big Build, secret compensation payments to a female prisoner assaulted by a male inmate in a women’s prison, and ongoing questions surrounding Daniel Andrews’ health and defamation proceedings. They also discuss growing concerns about police responses to protests against the visit of Israeli President Isaac Herzog last week. Discover more from Tim at The Unshackled

youtube.title: ANDREW WEIDEMANN
youtube.summary: Wind Turbines entering Australia as a result of National and State governments renewable energy targets have been found to be contaminated with asbestos. For more information check out Across Victoria Alliance on Facebook

youtube.title: SUE GREY
youtube.summary: Meagan McNamara reports from day two of Dr Caroline Wheeler’s Health Practitioners Disciplinary Tribunal in Nelson, over allegations she prescribed ivermectin in 2021—despite claims no patients were harmed and she’s faced years of stress and disruption. Lawyer Sue Grey, attending the hearing simply as a spectator, frames the case as part of a wider pattern of disciplinary action against clinicians who questioned COVID-era orthodoxy or explored alternatives. She describes an unusually supportive atmosphere, with more than 100 locals attending.

youtube.title: TECH TUESDAY
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan and Steven Sykes discuss a listener’s BNZ dispute after she refused app tracking and was effectively locked out of online banking, then stung with fees for in-branch alternatives. They also look at AI “caricature” trends as a Trojan horse for harvesting personal data, echoing early Facebook photo-tagging and today’s facial-recognition scale. Steven explains how aggressive AI web crawlers can swamp sites and why tools like Anubis are emerging to push back. They close on BitLocker’s cloud-stored recovery keys and what that means for real-world privacy. For everything you need to Say NO to Digital ID

youtube.title: MICHAEL REDDELL
youtube.summary: Independent economist Michael Reddell joins Paul to discuss the timing of the government's inquiry into decisions made by the Monetary Policy Committee at the RBNZ during Covid. He says New Zealand made the same mistakes central banks all over the world made during the pandemic. Discover more from Michael at Croaking Cassandra or follow him on X

youtube.title: NORA COFFEY
youtube.summary: Nora Coffey chats to RCR's Maree Buscke about common reasons for hysterectomy, stressing that surgery should be a last resort and that women need better access to comprehensive health information. They explore non-surgical alternatives, challenges around informed consent, the role of AI in medical education, and the growing demand for support from the HERS Foundation. For more information: Check out the Hers Foundation website or email for free information – hers@hersfoundation.org Watch Female Anatomy: The Functions of the Female Organs (What every woman wants and needs to know about female anatomy.)

youtube.title: RODNEY’S MAILBAG
youtube.summary: Rodney shares a heartfelt mailbag as listeners reflect on childhood innocence, Marxism, social conditioning and rediscovered Christian faith. Themes include love, gratitude, community, and the role of forgiveness in strengthening relationships. Click here to watch The Tribute

youtube.title: LARRY BLAIR
youtube.summary: Energy expert Larry Blair joins Paul to talk about why New Zealand is entering the “suddenly” phase of gas decline. Energy scarcity — not policy or ideology — is driving a fundamental economic shift, and the country’s industrial era of abundance is ending. They also talk about policy settings and plans for a new LNG terminal. For more information, check out New Zealand Energy on Substack

youtube.title: PAUL’S MAILBAG
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan sifts through a lively week of listener feedback, from Graham Hood’s cross-Tasman pushback on government control to strong reactions over Grant Dixon’s COVID documentary. Australia’s hate speech laws, climate policy, and the role of elected representatives spark debate, while health segments on low-carb diets and medical ethics draw praise. There's also comments on energy security, scepticism over AI healthcare and Trump’s ties to “Stargate.” Check out The Lila Rose Show – Separating Myth from Fact: A Common-Sense Understanding of V*ccines w/Dr Peter McCullough – Episode 287 Text your feedback to 2057 or email inbox@rcr.media And don't forget to follow us on Facebook and X

youtube.title: JILL OVENS
youtube.summary: Jill Ovens from the Women's Rights Party joins Paul to discuss a protest outside Western Springs College last week, against its policy of mandatory inclusion of boys in girls’ sports. For more information: The Women's Rights Party Learns That Gender Ideology Isn't Popular Amongst the Kids at Western Springs College Male Wrestler Accused of Sexually Assaulting Female Opponent During Girls Wrestling Match is Set To Compete in Washington State Championships The Women's Rights Party NZ

youtube.title: IVOR CUMMINS
youtube.summary: The Fat Emperor Ivor Cummins joins Paul for their first chat of 2026, covering the biggest story in the world right now: The Epstein Files. Ivor gives us his take on some of the most important revelations so far. They also discuss The Battle For Science conference in the Netherlands, which featured Dr Peter McCullough and Del Bigtree among others, and how the narrative around the safety of vaccines is starting to crumble. Discover more from Ivor at The Fat Emperor

youtube.title: WEEKLY ROUNDUP
youtube.summary: Dieuwe De Boer and William McGimpsey discuss immigration, energy security and economic developments in New Zealand, alongside political campaigning and surveillance concerns. They also cover international issues including grooming gangs, a Canadian school shooting and electoral integrity. For more information: Read William McGimpsey on The Zeitgeist NZ Substack or his RCR Blog Check out SpiderCat NZ – Crime In NZ or Who was behind the Bolshevik Revolution

youtube.title: MEDIA MATTERS
youtube.summary: Maree Buscke and Marty Gibson explore whether society is failing its children, discussing education, Oranga Tamariki, accountability, and family dynamics.
